small_guidance: The conv_transpose3d kernel uses 96 registers/thread limiting occupancy to 25-66%. Reduce register pressure: (1) hoist the IC loop to the outer level and use tl.dot with [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC] x [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_SP] tiles instead of scalar broadcasts, (2) add smaller-tile autotune configs like BLOCK_OC=16/BLOCK_SP=64 with num_warps=2 to raise occupancy, (3) remove the redundant fused_bn_meansub_kernel path (it runs after cuDNN BN already wrote output, doing duplicate work) — fold mean-subtract directly after BN in one pass.
large_guidance: Redesign as a scatter-add ConvTranspose3d: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), loading input once and scattering input×weight outer products into the output grid via atomic adds — this matches the natural data flow of transposed conv (stride=2 means most output positions only receive contributions from one input voxel, making the current gather over KD*KH*KW*IC with mostly-invalid strides extremely wasteful). Alternatively, reformulate as an im2col-style GEMM where the K dimension is IC*KD*KH*KW and use tl.dot with BLOCK_M=64 (OC), BLOCK_N=64 (output spatial), BLOCK_K=32, fuse BN affine (folded scale/shift from running stats) and per-(N,OC) mean-subtract into the epilogue (two-pass: first pass writes conv+BN and accumulates per-channel sum, second pass subtracts mean). Drop cuDNN BN entirely and fold BN running stats into a precomputed scale/shift at forward entry.
